_comment: The house's model management API (T-0278). Served by the manager inside jarvis-models (deploy/models/manager.py, port 8001, compose network only), relayed by the adapter under /api/models/* with the apps' bearer key, read by the console's Models panel (jarvis-web src/lib/hud/data/models.ts, route /settings/models). Every response is JSON; errors are {"ok": false, "error": "<sentence for a person>"} with a 4xx/5xx status. Both suites read this file: the manager's tests check that each example is what the endpoint returns for the fixture state, and the console's tests feed the examples through the mapper. A field added on one side without this file is a field the other side never sees.

list._comment: Every configured model, merged with llama-swap's /running and the download jobs. state: loaded | starting | unloaded | downloading | missing (configured but its weights are not on disk). settings are the editable vLLM flags parsed back from the model's file.

gpus._comment: Every card, what uses it and how much. who is a label per process: models (vLLM), voice (CosyVoice), hearing (Whisper), other. The console draws the budget from this, so nothing silently OOMs.

search._comment: Hugging Face, text-generation models, most downloaded first, at most 20. size_bytes is the sum of the repo's weight files (null when the Hub does not say). gated: the owner must accept a licence on huggingface.co first; the console says so and offers no download.

download._comment: Starts a download; an optional `file` (one .gguf, create_body.gguf_file) fetches only that file of a GGUF repo instead of the whole snapshot. With no `file` the manager takes it from its own config: the llama.cpp entry for that repo whose .gguf is not on disk, so a row whose file is gone is downloaded again by posting its repo alone (T-1269); a repo with no such entry downloads as a whole snapshot. A repo already downloading answers the running job, ok true. Refused (409, refusals.disk_full) when the repo's size is more than the free disk minus a 10 GB reserve, or (403, refusals.gated) when it is gated. Progress is read back from list.downloads; a download's state is running, done or error (error then carries the reason).

create._comment: Adds a model whose weights are on disk (engine and file: see create_body; llama.cpp writes a llama-server entry for that one .gguf and needs it linked in the cache): writes its llama-swap file (validated with llama-swap -validate before it replaces anything); llama-swap picks it up without a restart.

update._comment: Changes some settings; the rest keep their values. A loaded model is restarted by llama-swap with the new flags on its next request.

delete._comment: Removes the model's file (and records it, so the seed never brings it back); weights=1 deletes its weights from the cache too.

load._comment: Loads now (swapping out whatever else holds the cards) instead of on the next request. `gpus` is where it lands: per card, what a vLLM model needs (gpu_memory_utilization x total) and what is free once llama-swap's current model swaps out; need_mib is null for llama.cpp, and the list is empty for a model already running or on the CPU. A vLLM model that cannot fit is refused 409, naming the card and who holds it.

create_body._comment: What the add form sends to create (T-0512). engine is vllm (the whole snapshot, the default) or llama.cpp, which serves ONE .gguf of the repo and so needs `file`; a vLLM add sends no file. settings for llama.cpp are max_model_len, keep_loaded and idle_unload_s only. The same rule file applies to POST /downloads' optional `file`. Both suites read this table: the manager refuses what the rule refuses and the console's form says the same sentence before the round trip.

gguf_file.error: file is one .gguf in the repo.
gguf_file.shard_error: That file is one shard of a split GGUF; only a single .gguf file is supported.
gguf_file.missing_error: Pick the .gguf file to serve: llama.cpp reads one file of the repo.

refusals._comment: The sentences a create or a download is refused with (T-1269), by key: the HTTP status and a message whose {name} slots the caller fills. The manager (deploy/models/manager.py, which ships this file in the image) and the e2e mock (tests/web/mock-hermes.mjs) both format from here, so a reworded sentence is one edit. A response is still {"ok": false, "error": <the message>}: nothing in the console branches on the text, only on the status or the shape. The GGUF file sentences are create_body.gguf_file's. Not refusals: a download of a repo that is already downloading answers the running job with ok true.

repo_invalid.message: That is not a Hugging Face repo (owner/name).

id_invalid.message: The id is lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore.

file_on_vllm.message: file is for a llama.cpp model: a vLLM model serves the whole repo.

gated.message: {repo} is gated: accept its licence on huggingface.co first.

model_exists.message: There is already a model called {id}.

disk_full.message: {repo} needs {need_gb} GB and only {free_gb} GB is free once {reserve_gb} GB is kept back.

new_model_defaults._comment: A new model's settings when the request leaves one out (manager) and the add form's starting values (console).
